Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic SUV and Coupe Heads to Land Down Under With PHEV For the First Time
24 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
The premium German automaker's Australian division has announced a new addition to the Mercedes-Benz GLE roster, the first plug-in hybrid addition to the family: the GLE 450 e 4Matic with both SUV and Coupe body styles.
On an international level, Mercedes is preoccupied with announcing that the renowned Mercedes-Maybach S-Class individualized by LeBron James through Manufaktur Made to Measure is heading to auction for a good cause. A near-identical twin to LeBron James’ personal Maybach S-Class will be offered through Gooding & Christie’s at Retromobile New York in November, with proceeds from the auction to benefit the LeBron James Family Foundation and its ‘I Promise’ program.
But over in the Land Down Under, Mercedes-Benz Australia has more prosaic news: in September they announced the Mercedes-AMG G 63 Two-Finish Edition, the opening of Mercedes-Benz Studio Sydney, the facelifted EQS Sedan, the new launch of the premium transfer service with Qantas, as well as the all-new GLB compact crossover SUV, and now they finally have something fresh for October, too.
So, meet the Australian versions of the new Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic plug-in hybrid SUV and Coupe models which “bring electrified performance to the GLE range.” They combined a 3.0-liter inline-six gasoline engine with electric driving thanks to a 135 kW (181 hp) PSM electric motor. The combined output is 320 kW and 680 Nm, or 429 hp and 502 lb-ft of torque, and power delivery is through standard all-wheel drive and a 9G-Tronic automatic transmission.
Most importantly, the new model also has a 25.7 kWh usable high-voltage battery, so the GLE 450 e features a WLTP-tested electric range of 87 km for the SUV and 91 km for the Coupe, which is 54 and 57 miles, respectively. Electric driving can happen at up to 140 kph or 87 mph, which means that both “shorter everyday trips and freeway journeys can be completed without the petrol engine.”
The Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 e 4Matic plug-in hybrid model has all the goodies introduced with the recent mid-cycle refresh of the model family, and this version comes with standard 20-inch AMG five-spoke alloys for the SUV and 21-inch AMG five-twin-spoke rims for the Coupe. AMG Line exterior styling and the Night Package also come standard on the GLE 450 e.
Moving inside, the PHEV model gets heated front seats and an Artico man-made leather interior trim, a standard AMG Line Sport Seats Package upholstered in Artico with Microcut microfiber inserts in black, the MBUX Superscreen with three 12.3-inch displays tucked under a single glass surface, and the Mercedes‑Benz Operating System (MB.OS) with over-the-air updates.
Pricing kicks off at AU$156,900 (MRLP) and AU$160,900 (MRLP), for the SUV and Coupe, respectively. That’s almost $109k and over $111k at the current exchange rate, by the way.
